verdict.text:
## Summary
The model treats an unnamed system as a missing slot. In 15 of 35 requirements it emits `<MISSING_ACTOR>`/`<MISSING_MODAL_VERB>` where the annotators inferred "the App must". That over-flagging drives the incomplete-verdict false positives and most Paska failures. The headline scope/condition fabrication counts are likely a scoring artifact, not invented content.

## Missing-slot detection
Scope and condition look like fabrication, with flag rates of 0.24 and 0.29, but the outputs do not support that reading. 4031, 4333, 2943 and 496 contain no scope or condition text at all, yet are scored "filled". The model simply omits the optional placeholders, and the parser reads absence as filled. Until that is fixed, the 26 scope and 15 condition "silent fills" say little about fabrication.

Actor and modalVerb are the real failure, in the opposite direction from the risk the experiment probes. Each has one gold-missing case, both caught. The cost is 12 and 15 false flags on implied slots, so precision is 0.06–0.08. Chain-of-thought appears to reason "the source never names the system", which is stricter than the gold convention.

Action is the only slot with genuine fabrication. 496 invents "allow the user to change the maximum size of MMS", and 1504 also fills a gold-missing action. Both errors are defensible from the request titles. With 4 gold-incomplete requirements, the 0.75 verdict recall is one miss (496) and moves in 25-point steps.

## Conversion quality
Cosine sits close to the human-human ceiling (0.69 vs 0.74), so meaning is largely preserved. Sequence ratio (0.53 vs 0.64) and Jaccard (0.38 vs 0.49) trail further. Part of that gap is surface form: humans always write the `<MISSING_SCOPE>, <MISSING_CONDITION>,` prefix and the model drops it.

Paska failures are mostly placeholder fallout:
- All 14 "Not requirement" smells fall on outputs with a missing actor or modal.
- All 5 "Incomplete system response" smells are a missing modal (245, 6031, 1283, 937, 42-Mastodon).
- Pass rate is 0.76 when the model judges a requirement complete and 0.11 when it judges it incomplete.

Only five substantive smells remain: condition after response (6459, 828), non-atomic (6457), passive voice (828) and an imprecise verb (7310).

## Anomalies
- **Format breach in 757-Signal:** 43 characters outside the answer block and a stray `<rimay>` line. Its actor is gold-present but scored missing, so check whether the breach corrupted parsing.
- **Atomic requirements flagged `<NON_ATOMIC>` in 1504-Signal and 2055-Signal:** 2055 also fails Paska as "Incomplete requirement". Two of 35 cases is too few to shift headline metrics, but it shows the CoT prompt invites atomicity judgements on the atomic task.

## Next step
- Fix slot extraction so that omitted scope/condition placeholders count as missing, or require all five placeholders in the prompt. Then rescore Track 1 before drawing any fabrication conclusions.
- Add a prompt rule that an unnamed system defaults to "the App" with modal "must". Rerun and check whether the false actor/modal flags and "Not requirement" smells collapse.
- Compare against zsl/fsl on the same 35 requirements to test whether the over-flagging is specific to CoT.
